title: Ride the news
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What is happening this week that your customers care about?
I said that news-driven content uses the momentum of the news. I compared it to a bait ball, sardines gathered together, and the fish that come to feed on it.
I said that my own field is closely tied to flooding, so with a storm on its way, a company can speak about rainfall and what people should do, because everybody is already paying attention.
I said that calendar-driven content is about seasons, holidays and key dates for your audience, and that I like it when a business sends a birthday message.
A student said that current events are more helpful than news, and gave the example of a brand that posted when the lights went out in a stadium.

I said that you must be careful with your analysis and insight on the news, because you do not know what audience you have, and I am careful because people on my list have the full spectrum of political views.
I said that in a crisis you can give an objective view of the data, such as the dangers and the balance sheets.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the news your customers care about this week.
Write how your service helps with it.
Write the dates in your year that matter to them.
Write what you will not comment on.
Write your next post that rides the news.

check.q: What did I compare news-driven content to?
What did a student say is more helpful than news?
What did I say to be careful about?
choices: Your analysis, because you do not know your audience

recap: Use the moment's attention. Add dates. Be careful what you comment on.
